t1.text: Account: one unticked box for pictures

n1.text: New on A and B: the second box, Share pictures of cards I correct. Never ticked from the start, and not needed to continue: only the terms box unlocks the button. Asked once per account; after that it lives in Settings. The fine print is new: To find and fix problems, Mesa notes how the app is used and any errors. No ads, and no pictures unless you choose. On B a short What's new box says why the terms changed.

n2.text: Settings is new: Home's menu had only Sign out. The switch saves at once, with no Save button. Off means nothing new is kept from that moment. Delete removes every report and picture the player has sent, whatever the switch says, and leaves the switch as it is. No green toast: the result is written in place (F).

t3.text: Where the button sits, and what it is called

v1.text: V1 wins: nothing new on screen. It sits where people look for help (the menu) and where camera trouble shows (the panel). Loses: two clicks, and a player who never opens either won't find it.

v2.text: V2 wins: one click, always in sight, so every player learns it exists. Same label everywhere: Report a problem. On the phone it sits in the top bar beside Disconnect, not as a floating button that can be hit while placing the phone. Loses: one more control on the top bar.

t4.text: The report: what went wrong, which card, Send

n4.text: Nothing is required: Send works with no note and no tag, because the 10 minutes are the report. One tag at a time; tap again to clear. The sentence about what is sent changes when the phone is gone (L) and on the phone (M). The phone never sends by itself: a tap there asks the computer to send the same package (N), and says so when it can't (O). The code is a receipt the player needs, not an ok toast.

n5.text: The table the prompt calls section 4 is section 2 in today's privacy.html (section 4 is transfers). The draft changes sections 2, 3, 5, 6 and 7, and the version line. Anthropic is not changed: no new way sends pictures to Claude. Legal basis per row and the sentence about trained models are for Jesper to approve.

n6.text: G2: seven categories that match what goes wrong on the mat. Pointing at the card in the picture frozen at the press tells the reader which card. Wrong name asks what the card is called. It happened: Just now or Earlier tells the reader where in the 10 minutes to look. Only the category picks are new; Send still works with nothing filled in. States H to O get the new texts once G2 is chosen.

t6.text: Which card, and when: point at it

r1.text: R1 wins: tap first, then say what is wrong; the choices follow where you tapped (a card only in the camera can only be Didn't show up). A pin shows on both pictures, so the reader sees the same card twice. Loses: only shows the moment of the press; a problem that already went away can't be pointed at.

r2.text: R2 wins: everything in R1, plus a strip of the last minutes. Drag back to when it looked wrong and point there. Handles a duplicate that flickered and went away, or a card you already fixed. Loses: one more row; the mat in the strip comes from the computer's own history, the camera pictures from the phone's stills (MES-366), fetched when the box opens.

r3.text: R3 wins: no pictures to search; a list of what Mesa did, with your own fixes marked. Tap the line that went wrong. Very exact for the reader. Loses: a card that never showed up is not in the list (needs the camera picture below), and a list is harder to scan than a picture during a game.

t6b.text: New version: one problem, mark any cards

s1.text: S1: three steps, same order every time. 1 What went wrong (one category). 2 Which cards: tap any number, in the camera picture and on the mat, each picture on its own; numbers follow the order you tap. The strip picks the moment. 3 Anything to add, where the numbers can be used. One report is one problem; several problems are several reports (Report something else after sending). Nothing is linked between the pictures and nothing is asked per card, so there are no special cases. Only Wrong name asks one more thing: what the card is called.

s3.text: S3 is not something the player sees. It is the top of LÄS-MIG.md that dev/rapport/hamta.cjs writes (MES-365): category, the moment, every mark with its track and what Mesa did with it, the note, and the events around the moment. The marks turn the player's numbers into track ids, so the note can't be misread.

t6c.text: Third version: find it, mark it, then say what

tn.text: T1 in two steps. Step 1: pick the moment in the strip; the mat and the camera picture below follow it, so you look for the moment where the cards were wrong. Then tap the cards, on the mat, in the camera, or both. Step 2: what went wrong, and Your report: a sentence Mesa writes from your choices (category, moment, which numbers on the mat and in the camera). It only repeats what you picked and is not editable, so it can never put words in your mouth. The note is closed (+ Add a note) and is only for what the report doesn't say. A report with no note is still clear: the choices carry the meaning.

t7.text: The whole flow: playing, the mistake, the report

w0.text: Each board starts in a game. Press Next in the dashed bar: you play Island, Mesa shows it twice, the extra one goes away by itself. Then press Report a problem in the top bar and report it. Start over to try again with other answers.

w1.text: W1: a dialog in three steps. 1 What went wrong, as seven big buttons with a line each ("A card on the mat isn't on your table"), so the names never need explaining. 2 Show it: the instruction follows the answer, then the list of changes on your mat, and the mat and camera at the moment you pick. 3 Your report, written from your choices, and Send. Wins: the order people think in, one question per screen. Loses: three steps, and the pictures are small copies of the mat.

w2.text: W2: no dialog. The mat itself goes back in time, with a timeline of every change under it and the camera picture in the corner. You tap the cards on the real mat. A side panel asks what went wrong and writes your report. Wins: you recreate the mistake exactly where you saw it. Loses: the game is hidden while you report, and it is the biggest thing to build.

w3.text: W3: like W1, but after the answer Mesa shows the moment it thinks you mean, with the card ringed (here: the Island that came and went). Yes sends it in two taps; No opens Show it from W1. Wins: fastest when Mesa guesses right. Loses: a wrong guess that people accept without looking makes a wrong report; needs a rule for what Mesa suggests per answer.

t8.text: Simple report: say what you saw, point where

x0.text: Play X1: Next three times (you play Island, Mesa shows it twice, the extra one goes away), then Report a problem.

x1.text: One box, on top of the game, not over the whole mat. Your own words first and biggest; the example shows that time goes in the words (a minute ago...). Quick picks below, written as what you see, and they never change the box. Then Send. Where and When are not asked (Jesper 2026-10-13): Mesa saves the time of the press and what was on your screen (zoom, the part of the mat in view, the card you last touched), and the last 10 minutes. Nothing is required except Send.

x3.text: The work happens at the desk, not in the game. hamta.cjs puts the player's words on top, then Mesa's log for the part of the mat that was on screen in the last 90 s (this is where showed up and went away belong), then the events that fit the quick pick and the words, and the pictures. A person or Claude Code reads it as it is.

x4.text: On the phone: the same words and quick picks, then Send. Nothing to point at.

t8b.text: Which cards: a field that follows the quick pick

x5.text: X5 opens already in the report with A card appeared that I didn't play picked; try other quick picks. A field shows under the quick picks, its label follows the pick (Which card disappeared?). Several cards: each becomes a small token with a cross. Suggestions in order: cards that were on your mat in the last 10 minutes, with a short hint (left the mat 30 s ago) so two Islands can be told apart and the reader knows which one; then your deck; typing searches all cards. A card never showed up suggests your deck first. Wrong name is a pair, Mesa showed and it is, with + Another card. Everything stays optional.

y0.text: Same box as X1 in every state: your words, quick picks, Send. The box stays open while it sends (a few seconds). The receipt shows the code with its own Copy button and Done alone. If sending fails, your words are kept until the box is closed. The limit shows as soon as the box opens. Without the phone the report goes from the computer, without the phone's pictures. The phone never sends by itself; X4 is its box, Y6 and Y7 its receipt and its error. Replaces G to O on page 4.

l4.text: Reading a report, and the privacy text

l0.text: The latest of every screen, copied from the pages where it was decided: account and settings from pages 1 and 2, the button from page 3 (V2), the report box from page 8 (X1) with its states Y1 to Y7, the reader view (X3) and privacy.html from page 5. The privacy draft now also names what was on your screen when you pressed. Pages 1 to 8 stay as the history.
